Official estimates: trends and maps

Source: vignettes/maps-and-trends.Rmd
maps-and-trends.Rmd

Everything in this article works straight after installing bdhs. You don’t need a DHS account or any downloads, because the package ships every official estimate the DHS Program publishes for Bangladesh. These are the numbers in the BDHS final reports and in STATcompiler.

library(bdhs)

What is bundled

bdhs_indicators holds about 310,000 official values. That covers every indicator, every survey round from 1993-94 to 2022, and every published breakdown: national, division and background characteristics such as residence, education and wealth. bdhs_indicator_catalog describes each indicator (definition, denominator, topic and the rounds it covers).

nrow(bdhs_indicators)
#> [1] 310528
dplyr::count(bdhs_indicator_catalog, topic, sort = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 21 × 2
#>    topic                          n
#>    <chr>                      <int>
#>  1 Family Planning              366
#>  2 Child Health                 271
#>  3 Child Nutrition              216
#>  4 Household Characteristics    195
#>  5 Reproductive Health          189
#>  6 Water and Sanitation         160
#>  7 Fertility                    151
#>  8 Education                    141
#>  9 Infant and Child Mortality   137
#> 10 Women's Empowerment          115
#> # ℹ 11 more rows

Finding an indicator

bdhs_search() looks through indicator labels and definitions, survey variables and harmonized variables at once. Restrict it to indicators with where = "indicators":

bdhs_search("stunt", where = "indicators")
#> # bdhs search for "stunt": 2 matches
#> 
#> ── Official DHS indicators (2) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> CN_NUTS_C_HA3  Children severely stunted  1996-97, 1999-00, 2004, 2007, 2011, 2014, 2017-18, 2022
#> CN_NUTS_C_HA2  Children stunted           1996-97, 1999-00, 2004, 2007, 2011, 2014, 2017-18, 2022

Pulling official values

bdhs_official() returns tidy rows for one or more indicators. By default it gives the national headline value for every round:

bdhs_official("CN_NUTS_C_HA2")[, c("year_label", "indicator", "value", "ci_low", "ci_high")]
#> # A tibble: 8 × 5
#>   year_label indicator        value ci_low ci_high
#>   <chr>      <chr>            <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 1996-97    Children stunted  60.1     NA      NA
#> 2 1999-2000  Children stunted  51.1     NA      NA
#> 3 2004       Children stunted  50.6     NA      NA
#> 4 2007       Children stunted  43.2     NA      NA
#> 5 2011       Children stunted  41.3     NA      NA
#> 6 2014       Children stunted  36.1     NA      NA
#> 7 2017-18    Children stunted  30.8     NA      NA
#> 8 2022       Children stunted  23.6     NA      NA

Ask for a breakdown to get subgroup values, for example by division in 2022:

stunting_div <- bdhs_official("CN_NUTS_C_HA2", survey = 2022, breakdown = "subnational")
stunting_div[, c("characteristic_label", "value", "denom_unweighted")]
#> # A tibble: 11 × 3
#>    characteristic_label value denom_unweighted
#>    <chr>                <dbl>            <dbl>
#>  1 Barishal              24.9              496
#>  2 Chattogram/Sylhet     27               1278
#>  3 Chattogram            24.7              732
#>  4 Sylhet                33.9              546
#>  5 Dhaka before 2015     23.2             1132
#>  6 Dhaka                 21.5              607
#>  7 Mymensingh            27.7              525
#>  8 Khulna                19                450
#>  9 Rajshahi/Rangpur      21.1              904
#> 10 Rangpur               22.1              491
#> 11 Rajshahi              20                413

Besides the eight current divisions, the DHS Program also publishes the older groupings, such as “Chattogram/Sylhet”, “Dhaka before 2015” (Dhaka plus Mymensingh) and “Rajshahi/Rangpur”. These match the division layout of earlier rounds, so they are the values to use for long-run regional trends.

The survey argument accepts years, year ranges, DHS ids and file codes, so 2017, "2017-18", "BD2017DHS" and "7R" all mean the 2017-18 survey.

Trends

bdhs_plot_trend() draws an indicator across all rounds. Give it a characteristic category to split the trend:

bdhs_plot_trend("FE_FRTR_W_TFR", by = "Residence")

Several indicators can share one chart:

bdhs_plot_trend(c("CN_NUTS_C_HA2", "CN_NUTS_C_WH2", "CN_NUTS_C_WA2"))

Maps

bdhs_boundaries() returns the division boundaries used by a given survey, as an sf object. They come from the DHS Program Spatial Data Repository under the Open Database License. The number of divisions changed over time: 5 in 1993-94, 6 from 1996-97, 7 from 2011 (Rangpur) and 8 from 2017-18 (Mymensingh).

b <- bdhs_boundaries(2022)
b[, c("region_code", "region_name")]
#> Simple feature collection with 8 features and 2 fields
#> Geometry type: MULTIPOLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 88.03243 ymin: 20.59039 xmax: 92.68078 ymax: 26.63625
#> Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84
#>   region_code region_name                       geometry
#> 1           1    Barishal MULTIPOLYGON (((90.33083 21...
#> 2           2  Chattogram MULTIPOLYGON (((91.85583 21...
#> 3           3       Dhaka MULTIPOLYGON (((89.35535 23...
#> 4           4      Khulna MULTIPOLYGON (((89.2995 21....
#> 5           5  Mymensingh MULTIPOLYGON (((89.64786 25...
#> 6           6    Rajshahi MULTIPOLYGON (((88.7203 24....
#> 7           7     Rangpur MULTIPOLYGON (((88.83978 25...
#> 8           8      Sylhet MULTIPOLYGON (((90.96542 25...

bdhs_map() draws an official indicator by division:

bdhs_map("CN_NUTS_C_HA2", survey = 2022)

It also maps your own estimates. Any data frame with division codes (v024, hv024, region_code) or division names works, including the output of bdhs_estimate(..., by = "v024").

Notes on comparability

  • Division layouts differ between rounds, so division-level trends are only comparable after back-mapping to a common layout. bdhs_regions gives the crosswalk, and bdhs_harmonize() creates division_trend6 and division_trend5 for microdata.
  • Official values are rounded the way the DHS Program publishes them. Values you compute from microdata with bdhs_estimate() keep full precision.
  • Please cite the DHS Program API when you use these values (citation("bdhs")).
